references.text: Command not to appear before the Lord empty-handed, which is the basis for the principle of giving according to one's ability.
The Israelites gave voluntary gifts to the tabernacle as their hearts moved them, an example of giving according to one's ability.
The principle of giving the best of what one has received from the Lord.
Encouragement to bring offerings and appear before the Lord, in line with giving according to the Lord's blessing.
The people gave generously from the firstfruits because the Lord had blessed them, an example of giving proportionally to the blessings received.
Paul teaches that a gift is good when given according to one's ability, the same principle found in Deuteronomy 16:17.
The principle of sowing generously to reap generously, and to give cheerfully as each has decided in their heart.
The disciples decided to send help, each according to their ability, directly reflecting the principle in Deuteronomy 16:17.
